If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overreaction.  
If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
In mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33), apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to align with historical mean reversion.  
In late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is positive (≥0.67), apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to capture momentum, but cap at 3% to avoid overfitting.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.33) in the last 3 days, apply a 1.0–2.0% correction in mid-horizon to dampen volatility.  
If forecast deviates >3% from true value in early horizon and sentiment is neutral, apply a 1.0–1.5% downward correction to reduce overconfidence.
